case_scope: United States childcare cost, availability, and time-wealth interruption

household_market_extraction_gate.note: Childcare price data and cross-country net-cost indicators show care can be a household tollgate as large as rent or a major share of disposable income.

childcare_cost_time_wealth_drag.note: Certification requires local price, supply, hours-fit, subsidy, and net-cost evidence; average income or parent employment does not prove wealth formation.

childcare_labor_force_interruption.note: Census working-paper evidence links higher childcare costs to lower maternal labor-force participation, with lower-income mothers more responsive.

workplace_power_gate.note: Care gaps interact with scheduling, hours, and advancement.

claim_conversion_friction.note: Subsidies convert only if parents can find a slot matching work hours and do not lose eligibility at income cliffs.

care_market_availability.note: Price must be paired with local supply, waitlists, age slot, hours, provider stability, and quality constraints.

proof_debt: county-level price, supply, and age-slot availability
waitlists, hours fit, commute fit, and nonstandard-schedule availability
subsidy eligibility, cliff, reimbursement, and provider acceptance
parental quits, reduced hours, promotion refusal, and earnings loss
provider wage, turnover, quality, and closure risk
family backup dependence and unpaid-care spillovers

gate_16_household_market_extraction.why: Childcare is a blocked household-market-extraction surface unless net price, supply, hours fit, and subsidy conversion are proven at local threshold moments.

gate_14_workplace_power.why: Care costs can wash out labor-force participation and advancement; worker power cannot pass without care infrastructure evidence.

evidence_debt_register.question: county-level price, supply, and age-slot availability
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Use the DOL NDCP plus local licensing/supply data to prove whether care exists at threshold moments, not just whether a median price is known.

evidence_debt_register.question: waitlists and hours fit
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Measure availability for infant/toddler/preschool slots, nonstandard hours, commute-compatible locations, and backup care.

evidence_debt_register.question: subsidy eligibility and cliff conversion
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Score take-up, reimbursement adequacy, provider acceptance, income cliffs, and administrative delay.

evidence_debt_register.question: labor-force and earnings interruption
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Track quits, reduced hours, foregone promotions, job search constraints, and heterogeneous effects for lower-income mothers.

evidence_debt_register.question: provider stability and quality
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Measure provider wages, turnover, closures, quality constraints, and supply fragility that can turn subsidy into unusable paper support.

evidence_debt_register.question: family backup dependence
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Estimate unpaid kin-care reliance, grandparents/relatives labor effects, and cross-household transfer burden.

policy_pathway: Treat childcare as a conversion rail for work and savings, not a side expense.
Require local slot availability, net-cost caps, stable providers, subsidy conversion, nonstandard-hours support, and income-cliff protection before moving Gate 16 downward.
